transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. Thanks for coming in today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um... well, what brings me in is that I keep making myself throw up after I eat. I just... I do it a lot. Sometimes I'll use the bathroom at the laundry where I work, or I'll do it right when I get home. I really hate it, but... it's kind of started feeling like it's the only way I can actually calm down.
Before you make yourself throw up, do you typically eat a very large amount of food in a short period of time while feeling like you can't stop or control it?

Yeah, I do. Um, when it happens, I can just go through a full bag of chips, some pastries from the corner store, whatever leftovers I have, and a bunch of sweet drinks all in one sitting. It just happens so fast... I don't even really notice how much is gone until I'm done. It definitely feels like I can't stop once I start.
How often would you say this binge-eating and vomiting cycle happens, and how many months has it been going on at that frequency?

Well, it's been going on for a while now. I'd say for months, really. Most weeks, there are at least... maybe eight or nine times where I end up eating way more than I meant to. And then, you know, I try to undo it. Usually by throwing up, but sometimes I'll just not eat anything the next day, or I'll try to exercise really hard to burn it off. But yeah, it's pretty much every week, multiple times a week.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating (rapid consumption of large amounts of food with subjective loss of control) occurring multiple times per week for several months, followed by compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting, fasting, and excessive exercise to prevent weight gain. This pattern, with frequency exceeding once weekly for over 3 months, meets criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) rather than other feeding/eating disorder subtypes.

Purging behavior described as a way to 'calm down', suggesting emotional regulation function tied to eating behavior
